insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified in this excerpt (tables shown for multiple Basic Sum Insured options from ₹1,50,000 to ₹25,00,000 under base/Gold plan)

good.name: PED waiting period: 36 months (GOOD as per rules)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-Existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer
good.reference: Section IV (Exclusions) > 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code Excl 01 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage. As per the given rules, 36 months is still considered GOOD (not a red flag).

good.name: Specific illness/procedure waiting period: 24 months (GOOD)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.
good.reference: Section IV (Exclusions) > 2. Specified disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: Listed specific diseases/procedures are covered after 24 months, which is industry-standard.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days (GOOD)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Section IV (Exclusions) > 3. 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: A standard initial waiting period of 30 days applies for illnesses (accidents covered immediately).

good.name: Restore benefit: 200% once (unrelated illness only) (GOOD)
good.quote: There shall be automatic restoration of the Basic Sum Insured by 200%, once during the policy period... such restored Basic Sum Insured can be utilized only for illness / disease unrelated to the illness / diseases for which claim/s was / were made.
good.reference: Section II (Coverage) > K. Automatic Restoration of Basic Sum Insured (Page 3/9)
good.explanation: Sum Insured restores after exhaustion, but only for unrelated illnesses, so it is classified as GOOD (not best-in-class).

good.name: Co-pay: 10% for entry age 61+ (GOOD)
good.quote: This policy is subject to co-payment of 10% of each and every claim amount... for insured persons whose age at the time of entry in to this policy is 61 years and above.
good.reference: Important Note : Applicable for II Coverage and Optional Covers > Point 6 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: A 10% co-pay applying to those who enter at age 61+ is a common senior-citizen term and is considered GOOD.

bad.name: Room rent has daily cap (BAD)
bad.quote: 2% of Basic Sum Insured maximum of Rs.5,000/- per day
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > A. Room, boarding, nursing expenses... (Page 2/9)
bad.explanation: Room rent is capped (daily limit), which can lead to higher out-of-pocket expenses and can also trigger proportionate deductions on linked charges.

bad.name: Proportionate deduction applies due to room rent cap (BAD)
bad.quote: Expenses relating to Associated Medical Expenses will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent/room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > Note under A (Page 2/9) and definition of Associated medical expenses (Page 2/9)
bad.explanation: Because room rent is capped, the insurer can reduce payable amounts for associated expenses proportionately if you choose a higher room category than eligible.

bad.name: Pre-hospitalization: 30 days only (GOOD/BAD table => GOOD, but mandatory-report rule says report actual; here it is at the minimum end)
bad.quote: Pre-Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 30 days prior to the date of hospitalization
bad.explanation: Pre-hospitalization cover is limited to 30 days (minimum standard).

bad.name: Post-hospitalization: 60 days with additional cap (BAD because tight cap structure for post-hosp)
bad.quote: Post Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period up to 60 days... The amount payable shall not exceed the sum equivalent to 7% of the hospitalization expenses subject to a maximum of Rs.5,000/- per hospitalisation.
bad.explanation: Post-hospitalization is only 60 days (minimum standard) and also capped to 7% of hospitalisation expenses with a maximum ₹5,000 per hospitalization, which can be restrictive for follow-up medicines/tests.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (BAD)
bad.quote: ITEMS THAT ARE TO BE SUBSUMED INTO PROCEDURE CHARGES... DISPOSABLES RAZORS CHARGES... GAUZE... SURGICAL TAPE... (and similar lists of items to be subsumed)
bad.explanation: The policy provides lists of many items to be subsumed into package charges, but the wording provided does not explicitly state that common consumables (gloves, syringes, PPE kits etc.) are covered as a separate benefit. As per instructions, if consumables coverage is not clearly mentioned as covered, it is treated as not covered and flagged BAD.

bad.name: NCB/Cumulative Bonus reduces and can become zero on claim (BAD)
bad.quote: In the event of a claim... At any point of time, the cumulative bonus will not be less than “zero”. ... Full utilization of Basic Sum Insured and full utilization of cumulative bonus accrued, the cumulative bonus granted on renewal will be “nil” or “zero”
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > J. Cumulative Bonus (Base plan) Special Conditions (Page 3/9) and similar wording under Gold Plan (Page 4/9)
bad.explanation: The bonus is reduced when claims occur and can drop to nil/zero, meaning the Sum Insured growth is not protected on claims (a negative vs better policies where bonus is not reduced).

bad.name: Disease/treatment sub-limits (BAD) — Cataract and Modern Treatments
bad.quote: The expenses incurred on treatment of cataract are payable up to the limits mentioned hereunder; ... Coverage for Modern Treatments... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below;
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > H and I (Page 3/9) and detailed tables under Gold Plan (Pages 3-4/9)
bad.explanation: Sub-limits for cataract and modern treatments can leave significant costs payable by you if actual expenses exceed the stated limits.

unclear.name: Consumables coverage wording not explicit (verify if any consumables add-on/benefit exists)
unclear.quote: “Associated Medical Expenses” does not include cost of pharmacy and consumables, cost of implants and medical devices and cost of diagnostics, ICU charges and hence proportionate deduction will not be applicable on these items.
unclear.reference: Section I (Definitions) > Specific Definitions > Associated medical expenses (Page 2/9)
unclear.explanation: This line only clarifies that proportionate deduction (due to room rent) won't apply on consumables, but it does not clearly confirm that consumables are payable/covered under the policy. Confirm consumables coverage from the full policy wording/schedule or any add-on.

unclear.name: Cashless network size not stated (mandatory report item)
unclear.quote: Cashless facility can be availed only in networked Hospitals. For details of Networked Hospitals, the insured may visit www.starhealth.in or contact the nearest branch
unclear.explanation: The document does not mention the number of network hospitals, so the cashless network strength cannot be assessed from this excerpt.
